project: Hierarchical Human-Alignment Reproduction (given behavior + discovery mechanism)
direction: Distill hierarchical human-similarity structure (from THINGS triplets, via a SigLIP-So400m teacher) into pretrained vision backbones (DINOv2 ViT-B main) and test whether alignment improves multi-level human-similarity correlation, reproduces human behaviour/uncertainty, and preserves/improves downstream utility + OOD robustness.

claims.statement: THINGS-fit SigLIP-So400m teacher head has held-out THINGS triplet accuracy strictly above the unaligned SigLIP-So400m baseline AND above the 1/3 chance floor (bootstrap-CI-95 does not cross either comparator).
claims.origin: task.md Claim 1 (teacher captures human similarity structure well enough)
models: SigLIP-So400m (frozen backbone; small alignment head learned on THINGS train)
claims.method: Triplet-KL fit of an alignment head on frozen SigLIP-So400m image features; held-out triplet-choice accuracy vs. unaligned SigLIP + chance (M1) — screen step of the Screen → Decode → Verify → Recover composition (Parameter-Space Task Vectors family).

main_experiment.key_stats: teacher_triplet_acc=0.590 [0.582, 0.598] vs unaligned SigLIP=0.460 [0.452, 0.467] vs chance=0.333; Δ(teacher−unaligned)=+0.130 with non-overlapping CI95
main_experiment.headline: Teacher head strictly beats unaligned SigLIP + chance on held-out THINGS triplets (+13pp, non-overlapping CI95).

claims.final_status: ⚪ integrity_only (audit PASS; swap-test deferred — max_verify_claims cap)

claims.statement: The THINGS-fit teacher's triplet-choice signal on ImageNet-synthesised triplets is monotonically level-organised across coarse / mid / fine (each level above chance; ordering pre-declared).

data.source: ImageNet val + WordNet-hierarchy-derived synthesised triplets (leaf-parent construction for fine)

claims.method: Forward-only per-triplet choice-agreement rate at each hierarchy level (M2).

main_experiment.key_stats: coarse=0.750 [0.723, 0.777], mid=0.747 [0.720, 0.774], fine=0.817 [0.794, 0.840]; all > chance 0.333 but ordering is fine > coarse ≈ mid (not strictly monotonic)
main_experiment.headline: All three levels beat chance, but ordering is non-monotonic (fine best) — teacher separates fine-grained WordNet parents better than depth-2 coarse groups (likely SigLIP training-signal bias toward basic-level distinctions).

claims.final_status: ⚪ integrity_only WARN (numeric citation mismatch in fine-level; swap-test deferred — max_verify_claims cap)
caveats: The plan's strict monotonicity predicate may not match the natural ordering induced by SigLIP training data; reconsider the ordering claim rather than the per-level above-chance claim.

claims.statement: Alignment finetune of DINOv2 ViT-B against the THINGS-fit teacher increases aggregate Spearman correlation with human THINGS-triplet similarity by Δρ ≥ 0.05 over the unaligned DINOv2 ViT-B baseline, with paired-bootstrap significance at α = 0.05.

data.source: eval: THINGS held-out human triplets (1.71M pairs); finetune: ImageNet-val 50k pool (40k sampled, seed 42)
data.used_n: 40k for finetune; full THINGS held-out for eval
data.subset_note: Plan asked for 150k ImageNet-train subset; substituted with 40k of ImageNet-val (val was on disk) — cost-aware. Matched-cost between M3 and M5 preserved.

claims.method: M3 full-backbone KD finetune (triplet_kl loss, α=1.0, lr=5e-5, batch=512, 1 epoch, seed 42) of DINOv2 ViT-B against the M1 teacher on the ImageNet subset; then held-out THINGS Spearman vs. M4 unaligned baseline (paired-bootstrap α=0.05). Verify step of the Screen → Decode → Verify → Recover composition (Parameter-Space Task Vectors family).

main_experiment.key_stats: Δρ_aggregate = +0.366 (M3=0.555 vs M4=0.189), 7× the +0.05 threshold, non-overlapping CI95; triplet accuracy Δ = +0.125 (M3=0.556 vs M4=0.431).
main_experiment.headline: Alignment finetune produces a very large Spearman gain vs the unaligned DINOv2 ViT-B baseline (+0.366, 7× the required threshold).

claims.final_status: ✓ holds (PASS at verify: model-swap DINOv2 ViT-B → ViT-S also produces large Spearman gain Δρ=+0.324 vs main +0.366; robustness=1.00)
caveats: Absolute levels may shift under the plan's original 150k ImageNet-train pool; ranking direction and effect magnitude should hold.

claims.statement: The aligned DINOv2 ViT-B more accurately reproduces human behaviour AND per-triplet uncertainty than the unaligned baseline, conjunctively across three predicates: (i) higher per-triplet choice-agreement with humans, (ii) lower model-to-human uncertainty-KL AND higher rank correlation between model confidence and human agreement, (iii) higher RSA between model RDM and human RDM.

data.source: THINGS testset2.txt vs testset2_repeat.txt (two independent workers per triplet, row-aligned, ≥99.9% aligned)

claims.method: M6 forward-only behavioural + uncertainty comparison — per-triplet choice-agreement on human-consensus subset, human-agreement-Spearman rank correlation, model→human KL, model-RDM vs human-RDM Spearman; 3/3 predicates → established.

main_experiment.key_stats: choice_acc_on_agreed 0.586 vs 0.434 (+15.2pp); uncertainty_spearman 0.054 vs 0.017 (both weak, aligned direction correct); RSA_spearman 0.555 vs 0.189 (+0.366); KL(human→model) 0.228 vs 0.271 (supporting).
main_experiment.headline: All 3 predicates met — aligned reproduces human choice, uncertainty structure (weakly), and RDM (strongly).

claims.final_status: ⚪ integrity_only (audit PASS; swap-test deferred — max_verify_claims cap)
caveats: Uncertainty Spearman is weak in absolute terms (0.054 vs 0.017) — the binary two-worker agreement label is a sparse signal; direction is correct but strength is low.
